name: W copies its unit
summary: The state |0⟩ (a W-node without outputs) is copied by a W-node.
description:
The W-node (black triangle) with one input and $n$ outputs maps $|0\rangle \mapsto |0\cdots 0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \mapsto |10\cdots0\rangle + |010\cdots0\rangle + \cdots + |0\cdots01\rangle$: it spreads a single excitation over its outputs in all possible ways. The small dot marks its input leg. A W-node with no outputs is the state $|0\rangle$ (read as an effect, it is $\langle 0|$), which is the unit of the W-node read as a 'merge'.

Since the W-node sends $|0\rangle$ to $|0\cdots0\rangle$, plugging the unit into its input gives a copy of the unit on every output. This is the rule that makes the unit a comonoid homomorphism, one of the Hopf-algebra axioms of the W-node (axiom 5b of Hadzihasanovic).
parameter_notes: m is the number of outputs of the W-node (shown for m = 2); holds for any m.
